penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: A Quip bulk migration is inherently a project-scoped engagement: each customer has a unique document structure, folder hierarchy, and destination system. Configuring, running, monitoring, and validating the migration requires per-customer human involvement — at minimum reviewing outputs and handling edge cases. This is closer to a managed service engagement than a self-serve automated tool.

rationale: IT admins and Salesforce consultants migrating Quip libraries are a real buyer type with a genuine time-cost pain, and they do operate in a paid enterprise context. However, each migration is a one-time, project-scoped engagement with highly variable data structures — the actual work cannot be fully automated without per-customer configuration and validation, scoring operational_autonomy at 5 before the penalty. After the requires_human_fulfillment penalty, total drops to 3.3, well below the validate threshold. This is a consulting engagement disguised as a tool opportunity.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable for the autonomous factory model. A Quip migration service would require per-customer scoping (understanding their folder structure, target system, data mapping), running the migration with monitoring, and validating results — all of which are per-client manual work. Even a rate-limit-aware batching script would need to be customized and supervised for each client. This is better suited to a Salesforce consulting firm than a solo automated micro-service.
notes: Failing build_gates: operational_autonomy=5 (below min 7). Total 3.3 also well below min_total_to_validate=5.5 after requires_human_fulfillment penalty. Drop.
